heroHeadline: Senate Budget Committee Advances $71.7B ICE/CBP Reconciliation Package to Floor 11–10; DOJ Appoints 77 New Immigration Judges; 287(g) Reaches 1,843 Agencies; Record 73,000 in Detention
heroSubtitle: On May 20, 2026, the Senate Budget Committee voted 11–10 along party lines to send the $71.7 billion ICE/CBP reconciliation package to the full Senate floor — clearing the final procedural hurdle before a floor vote that Senate Republicans are racing to hold before Trump's June 1 signing deadline. The bill would fund 100,000+ detention beds, mass deportation flights, and a tripling of 287(g) local law enforcement partnerships, making it the largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history if enacted. On May 21, the DOJ/EOIR announced the appointment of 77 new immigration judges and 5 temporary judges in one of the largest single-batch expansions in immigration court history — with the administration having loosened qualification requirements to rapidly fill court vacancies. The 287(g) program has now reached 1,843 enrolled law enforcement agencies across 39 states and 2 territories as of May 19. ICE detention remains at a record 73,000+, with 30+ deaths in FY2026 custody and no oversight provisions in the reconciliation package.
footerNote: Data sourced from DHS, ICE official records, ACLU, HRW, DHS OIG, TRAC Reports, Detention Watch Network, USCIS, ILRC, NIPNLG, Human Rights First, court records, Senate Budget Committee, and Congressional records
